Key Activities: As part of the Area Management team, contributes to the development of operational plans for Census data collection activities; and manages census field and office operations for an LCO (7-day collection operation).

Manages the financial, human and material resources for the assigned LCO ; and manages the recruitment process for both Public Service Employment Act (PSEA) and Statistics Act employees required to meet the demands of a large temporary workforce.

Develops collections strategies and contingency plans; establishes and defines priorities; monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of LCO data collection systems and processes; analyzes and produces reports on the progress of the LCO activities; and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Monitors performance indicators; reports on the efficiency and effectiveness of LCO operations; and implements corrective action to resolve problems. Evaluates cost efficiencies, productivity and security of the Local Census Office.

Implements and provides expert interpretation of departmental legislation and the application of Statistics Canada policies and procedures; and leads the preparation and delivery of training to Assistant Manager, Field Operations, Assistant Manager Collection Unit, Assistant Manager Recruitment and Administration Officer.

Represents the department in consultations with the general public to solicit participation from non-respondents, responds to and resolves complaints; and contributes to public relations activities to promote Census Communications and respondent co-operation.
Represents the LCO in regional and/or department committees involved in the evaluation of the Census collection activities and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.
Disseminates and collects evaluation reports for the assigned LCO ; summarizes findings; and makes recommendations for program improvements.

Provides support to Regional administration with the opening of the office space such as visits during construction fit up, ensures office readiness for the beginning of field activities as well as closing down the LCO once operations have been completed.

Decision making: Effort is required to make decisions/recommendations on: the determination and definition of objectives, content and approaches for Census collection activities in the LCO and the operational framework and conditions within which the statistical program will occur; development and implementation of collection applications, alternate work methods and models to achieve desired outcomes; the development of strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes; the resolution of complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents; the development and distribution of guidelines, instructions and procedures for use by LCO Managers and staff; approval of appointments of all Statistics Act staff in the LCO region; the assurance that financial expenditures and resources are within allocated budgets; and the day-to-day management of financial, human and material resources of the LCO.
Decisions/recommendations taken affect the efficient and effective operations of the LCO and the LCO’s compliance to the Statistics Act and departmental policies and procedures.
Leadership and operational management: Manages the recruitment, development and retention of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce in the LCO. Establishes, coordinates and leads multi-disciplinary project teams and work groups comprising professional, technical, and administrative and Field Staff engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Approves work plans and priorities. Establishes organizational structures, assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and evaluates employee performance, provides training and guidance.
Monitors expenditures for staffing and material resources to ensure funds are spent appropriately and the LCO budget is respected.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the LCO in accordance with departmental policy and procedures, identifies content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, as well as professional fees.

Oversees some of the aspects related to the LCO fit up with local contractors to ensure readiness at time of opening and coordinate the dismantlement of the facility at the end of Census collection operation
Communication: Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from managers, employees to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes and briefings on LCO program results.
Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from the general public on the requirements for response, purpose of the Census or issues with employees.

There is an occasional requirement to respond to inquiries from the media. These situations are difficult as dealing with the media requires "thinking on your feet", as well as ensuring that statements made are clear so as not to be misunderstood.

Communications skills are also required to intervene and deal with uncooperative and sometimes hostile respondents. There is a requirement to "take control" over these emotionally charged situations, and persuade the respondent to take a more rational approach to a situation.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of socio-economic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs to manage the LCO field operations, analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand the need for new data and to assess the impact on collection activities and programs.
In-depth knowledge of statistical data collection methods, concepts and practices and survey operations to manage the activities of the LCO and to provide expert advice on data collection issues.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations and data quality), practices and classifications systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of Census activities.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management and of project management methods, techniques and practices to manage the work of a Local Census Office and organize, plan, schedule and control the LCO operational activities.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge and understanding of Statistics Canada’s mandate, programs, objectives, policies and procedures in areas such as survey methodology, operations integration, data confidentiality and security, dissemination and marketing to manage staff in the delivery of the program within a LCO and ensure that the work undertaken is standardized and consistent with departmental requirements.

Knowledge of the, regional and local operations’ mandate, activities, priorities, standards and procedures to the work to incorporate them into the management of the LCO and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, and respondent relations and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of Census activities.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act, Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act, Collective Agreementsand related policies and directives and supporting financial and human resources management methods, techniques and practices in order to manage the financial, human resource and material resources of assigned LCOs.
Research and analysis: Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes and proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.
Analyses the relative quality of data, researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures used, determines reasons for variances and initiates solutions.
Identifies and evaluates variations in survey responses and contributes to promotional activities to increase respondent participation rates.
Analyzes and produces reports on the progress of the LCO activites and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.
